items.text: Hypothesis: Re-keying order and product data between systems when Dahl's technical trade units are reconciled with Kesko's ordering and financial data — Public clue: Integrating the Dahl businesses (which keep separate brands and units) may require manual reconciliation of order and financial data across units. This is an inference from the acquisition announcement, not a confirmed internal process. (~12 h/week, estimate)

Hypothesis: Moving stock and order data by hand between warehouse, ERP and reporting tools during the rollout of a new cloud warehouse system across five distribution centres — Public clue: Manhattan Associates announced Kesko selected its ActiveWarehouse cloud warehouse solution; initial rollout covers five distribution centres. Data-transfer steps during migrations are a common manual load; this is an estimate of that load, not a confirmed Kesko workflow. (~8 h/week, estimate)

Hypothesis: Compiling and checking tender-related product and pricing lines for public-sector food and construction-material bids — Public clue: Kesko Oyj Kespro and Kesko Oyj appear as matched winners in several EU tender notices for frozen berries, industrial foods, construction materials and event services (name matches only, to be verified). Preparing and matching line items per tender is typically manual. (~6 h/week, estimate)

Hypothesis: Re-entering store-level and retailer-level changes (store renames, new K-Market owner records) across registers and internal records — Public clue: Kesko's register shows six name registrations in late 2025, including K-Market, Suomen Lähikauppa and Valintatalo, plus a new K-Market owner announced in October 2026 (Kotiharju, Joensuu). Each change touches several records. (~4 h/week, estimate)

Hypothesis: Handling 'Skannaa ja osta' and other new self-service channel data, such as mapping scanned-basket transactions to product master data — Public clue: K-ryhmä is promoting a new scan-and-go shopping method (#skannaajaosta, posted 2026-10-23). Adding new channels typically means manual mapping of product and transaction data in the short term; this is an estimate. (~5 h/week, estimate)

blocks.text: Estimate: Hours per week are rough estimates derived from the scale of each initiative and typical manual effort in comparable integrations and migrations, not from any Kesko internal data; the fte is the sum of those hours divided by 37.5, and eurPerYear is fte multiplied by an estimated loaded Finnish salary of €55,000. Public evidence only; the real numbers come from a conversation.

blocks.label: Note to the COO (with the card)
blocks.text: Hi [Name], I'm a writer at Velho, an AI growth partner for Finnish companies. Kesko's Dahl integration and the new warehouse rollout suggest a lot of order and data reconciliation may be landing on people's desks. We built a playful card of what that repetitive work could look like, with rough estimates attached. We're not claiming it's happening. Is there a ghost on your team doing this, and if so, would you like to see how we'd approach it?
